apiTokenHelp: Starts with abrk_. It belongs to exactly one client and is shown only once when it is created; a new one can be created and the old one revoked at any time.
feedinTableHelp: If a feed-in meter exists, the self-consumption is production minus feed-in. Without it, the smaller of production and total consumption is used.
flowConsumption: Consumption of the building per day in kWh
flowCountersNote: The source "Counters" has no Solar-Log mapping: the daily values come from the meter readings in the tables on the Counters tab (difference between two daily closings at 23:58).
flowFeedin: Feed-in in kWh: exact when the day was integrated over the day; otherwise production minus consumption (at least 0)
flowIntro: Which data points of the Solar-Log adapter (solarlog.0) are delivered to the billing server as which values. Daily values are delivered: the current day as a provisional state (every 15 minutes, computed by the solarlog adapter including the split into solar and grid power); at 23:58 the day is closed and replaces the provisional state. In addition the adapter asks the server every 10 minutes as a sign of life and delivers missing days afterwards.
flowMethod: Calculation method: "integriert" (integrated) when the polls cover at least 95% of the day, otherwise "tagesnetto" (approximation)
flowProduction: Production per day in kWh: daily yield of all inverters
flowQuality: Data quality: "veraltet" (outdated) when the last Solar-Log poll is more than 30 minutes old
flowSplit: Split of each unit's consumption into solar power and grid draw (from the integration over the day, otherwise daily net approximation)
flowTariffs: Tariffs are not delivered: the server provides them and the adapter takes them from there.
flowUnitConsumption: Consumption per unit in kWh: daily sum of the meter. <name> is the name of the unit (rename or skip it in the table on the Source tab)
flowUnitMeter: Meter reading per unit: running reading, maintained by the Solar-Log adapter
hintConnectionText: The adapter delivers the daily figures to the Abrechnung Mailcarrier web application over HTTPS. Server and token come from the Administration area of the web application (Clients, tab Access).
hostHelp: Host name only, e.g. abr.mailcarrier.ch. The connection is always encrypted (HTTPS).
hostInvalid: Enter only the host name, without path (e.g. abr.mailcarrier.ch).
journalStateIdHelp: State of the solarlog adapter with the daily journal (default solarlog.0.Database.dailyJournal). One entry per day with the daily values; the current day is updated provisionally every 15 minutes and closed at night.
metersTableHelp: One row per apartment: the name as it appears in the billing (e.g. WHG 1) and the energy state of its meter.
productionTableHelp: Energy states of the production of all inverters. They are added up.
snapshotTimeHelp: Time of day when the readings are taken and the day is closed (default 23:58).
snapshotTimeInvalid: Please enter a time as HH:MM.
sourceCounters: Energy states of other adapters (e.g. Shelly, inverter)
sourceType: Where do the figures come from?
sourceTypeHelp: iobroker.solarlog computes the split itself and keeps a local journal. With energy states the split is computed here from counters of other adapters.
staleMinutesHelp: A reading older than this at day closing marks the day as outdated.
unitMapTableHelp: Only needed if a unit of the solarlog journal must be called differently in the billing, or must not be delivered at all.
mbusIntro: Reads cold/hot water and heat meters through a Moxa serial server (TCP, raw mode) and delivers the readings to the web application. The Moxa addresses, intervals and the assignment of meters to apartments are maintained in the web application under Zähler (M-Bus) and transferred here. All readings are stored on the disk of this host first (adapter data folder, archive/) and delivered later if the connection fails.
mbusEnabledHelp: Server and API path are the same as on the Connection tab. The solar delivery is independent of this.
mbusTokenHelp: One token per site (client). It is created in the web application under Administration, API access; when a new site is created on the M-Bus tab it is shown once. The data points appear under mbus.a1, mbus.a2 ...
moxaPasswordHelp: Password of the NPort web console (15 characters at most). The adapter checks the firmware weekly and installs new versions at night between 01:00 and 02:45 if the web application allows it for that Moxa. Leave empty to switch the firmware care off. The password stays encrypted on this host.
mbusTablesHint: Moxas, apartments and routers can be entered here and in the web application. Both sides are compared as soon as M-Bus is switched on and a token is entered: new and changed rows go to the web application, changes made there appear here. After a comparison the instance restarts once. Column Site: a1 to a4 is token 1 to 4.
mbusMoxasHelp: One row per Moxa: address and port (Moxa in TCP server mode, raw, 4001) and the web password of this box (up to 15 characters, stays encrypted on this computer and is never sent to the web application). For every active Moxa the adapter mounts a virtual COM port automatically (column COM port, a file in the data folder of the instance), unmounts it when the Moxa is unreachable, disabled or deleted, and reconnects by itself after an outage. Without a web password the firmware of this Moxa is not looked after. If the Moxa is in the wrong mode (e.g. Real COM instead of TCP server) or set to the wrong serial line, the adapter sets it up through the web console (TCP server mode, raw, the port of the row, baud rate and parity of the site, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit) and restarts it when Set up is ticked.
mbusUnitsHelp: Name of the unit, e.g. WHG 1 or Allgemein 1. Single meters are assigned in the web application. A unit with assigned meters cannot be deleted here. Renaming means creating a new one.
mbusRoutersHelp: Routers in the house network the adapter updates over SSH (key: see tab Router in the web application). Updates run only on the chosen weekdays from the time on, within the window (minutes).
networkIntro: Network devices of the site: the Moxa serial servers (with an automatically mounted COM port and their own web password) and the MikroTik routers. Works together with the web application, see the note in the tab M-Bus Zähler.
mbusMetersHelp: The meters found on the bus. Kind, apartment (name from the table above), label and status can be changed here, as in the web application. Meters only come from a bus scan. Status ignoriert takes the meter out of the reading. Current readings are in the states under mbus.
mbusStatusButton: Show status (Moxa, COM port, firmware, routers)
mbusSettingsHelp: Per site: bus scan (assignment check, default 30 days), meter reading (minutes, default 15) and time sync (days, default off). Valid in the web application and here, both sides are compared. A scan runs once right after the Moxa was added (first scan, repeated hourly until it succeeds) and then only after the days have passed or on request in the web application.
